data.narrative:
Seneca operates in the Drones & Autonomous sector at Series A stage. The broader sector comprises eight private peers—including Waymo, Wayve, Zipline, Joby Aviation, and Nuro—with no public comparables available. The company has raised $60M to date.

Valuation analysis relies on stage-progression methodology, as peer-median triangulation proved inapplicable. The sector contains only seven same-sector peers; filtering by stage, timing, and valuation tier yielded fewer than three comparable datapoints, making median peer analysis unreliable. Stage-progression applies a 2.0x step-up multiplier typical for Series A advancement, producing an implied post-money valuation of $120M against the $60M capital deployed to date.

The analysis supports a valuation range of $102M to $138M, with a median point of $120M. This range reflects a 1.7x to 2.3x multiple on total capital raised, consistent with typical Series A-to-subsequent-round expansion in capital-intensive hardware and autonomy sectors. Key uncertainties include the absence of precise peer financials at comparable stage and the limited number of granular comps within the narrow Drones & Autonomous category. A fuller peer-based triangulation would require additional same-stage private transactions or public market data to validate this conclusion.
